clue.text: Saucy, for a time

parts.note: per means for a, as in 'ten pounds per head'

explanation.surface: Someone is cheeky only briefly, for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Pert describes a forward, impudent manner, a close synonym of cheeky.

clue.text: Expert's love for top American mailman?

indicators.note: love for top American means one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: a past master is an expert

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scores, so O

explanation.surface: A specialist prefers a leading American postal worker.
explanation.walkthrough: PAST MASTER (an expert) swaps its A, the top of American, for O (love): POST MASTER. The question mark flags that a postmaster runs a post office rather than delivering.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmaster is in charge of a post office, so loosely a mail worker; the query admits the stretch.

clue.text: Engineers and soldiers following soldier's rules

definitions.note: a regimen is a single set of rules, so the plural stands for one collective noun

indicators.note: following places the soldiers after the single soldier

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
GI is a US soldier
men are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Engineers and troops obey the regulations set by a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of conduct, diet or exercise: a set of rules to follow.

clue.text: Popular story about sick revolutionary is perfect

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the story goes about, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word for sick is read backwards

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A well-liked tale about an ailing rebel turns out to be flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ILL into LLI, and 'about' puts the story FABLE around it: FA-LLI-BLE, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Infallible means incapable of error, so without any flaw: perfect.

clue.text: Unacceptable to claim inventor's first idea

indicators.note: to claim means to take hold of, so the phrase captures the letter inside it

parts.note: not on is an idiom for unacceptable

indicators.note: first means the initial letter of inventor

explanation.surface: It is wrong to claim credit for the inventor's original idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is a British idiom for unacceptable; it holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief, so a synonym of idea.

clue.text: Essentially, tall locals patrol Maze prison

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so each word gives its middle letters

explanation.surface: The heart of the matter: tall local men guard the Maze prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maze was a Northern Irish prison; here it only supplies its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was the notorious federal prison on an island in San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: Allow John to start to investigate flies

indicators.note: flies means leaves quickly, so those letters depart from the word

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of investigate

explanation.surface: Permit John to begin looking into some flies.
explanation.walkthrough: John is the toilet; TO and I fly off it.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone do something is to permit or allow it.

clue.text: Relative nearly left establishment that struggles to maintain social distancing

definitions.text: establishment that struggles to maintain social distancing

indicators.note: nearly means not quite whole, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a brother is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative nearly gone from a venue that can't keep people apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke on pandemic rules: in a brothel people cannot keep their distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brothel is a house of prostitution, where close physical contact is the whole business.

clue.text: Worried, skipping question that's simple

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so the letters for question are dropped

parts.note: queasy can mean uneasy or troubled

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious and avoids the question because it's straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means requiring little effort, the same sense as simple.

clue.text: One's again hit hard following server issues during court proceedings

definitions.text: One's again hit hard following server issues during court proceedings

parts.words: One's again hit hard following server issues during court proceedings
parts.note: reads like a defendant battered by computer trouble in a law court, but the server is a tennis player, the court a tennis court, and the object struck again and again is the ball

explanation.walkthrough: 'server' suggests computers and 'court proceedings' a trial; on a tennis court the ball is served and then hit repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis ball is what the server puts into play and players keep striking during a rally.

clue.text: Regulate boxing agents, in part

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to set a clock or dial is to regulate it
G-men are US federal agents, from 'government men'

explanation.surface: A call to bring control to the agents who handle boxers, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport but means enclosing: SET holds GMEN. G-men is American slang for FBI agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one section or portion of a whole, so a part.

clue.text: They're positive half of defensive works must be removed

indicators.note: half of the long word is wanted here, the fourteen letters cut down to seven
removed tells us the front half is taken away, leaving the back half of the word

parts.note: fortifications are walls and earthworks built for defence

explanation.surface: Someone confidently says half the defensive works have to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They're positive' reads as people being sure; in chemistry it is the definition. FORTIFICATIONS has fourteen letters; dropping the first seven leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cations are ions carrying a positive electric charge, attracted to the cathode.

clue.text: In test, males frequently getting compassion in critical period

indicators.note: In before males places that word within the test

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK vehicles
men are males
oft is an old word for often
ruth is an archaic word for pity or compassion, surviving in ruthless

explanation.surface: During an exam, the men repeatedly show sympathy at a crucial stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness check for cars; ruth (compassion) survives today mainly in ruthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment of truth is the decisive point when something is put to the test: a crucial time.

clue.text: I bury someone who's passed in an unconventional manner?

definitions.text: I bury someone who's passed in an unconventional manner?

parts.words: I bury someone who's passed in an unconventional manner?
parts.note: the speaker deals with the dead and lays them in the ground; the query hints that the job title can also be read as someone who takes a test by going beneath rather than over

explanation.walkthrough: 'passed' means died here, though it tempts a reading of passing an exam or a ball. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker is a funeral director, who arranges the burial of the dead.

clue.text: Photograph last plant

parts.note: a snap is a quick photograph
to drag on is to last tediously long

explanation.surface: A picture taken of the final plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like an adjective for the plant, but is a verb: to drag on.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden flower whose blooms open like a mouth.

clue.text: Most balanced article on Sweden is in French

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means coming after, so the article follows Sweden

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
an is the indefinite article
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about Sweden, written in French, is the most level-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanest is the superlative of sane, meaning most mentally sound and even-tempered.

clue.text: Chap wearing trousers playing old musical instrument

indicators.note: used as a verb, trousers means pockets, so the pieces hold the other letters inside them

parts.note: a chap is a man
in means wearing, as in 'in a suit'

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of old are moved about

explanation.surface: A man in trousers plays some antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets: MAN IN takes DOL, from 'playing' acting on OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandolin is a small lute-like stringed instrument with paired strings, played with a plectrum.

clue.text: Team, one from Madrid, of stars

parts.note: a side is a sports team
Real Madrid is the famous football club, so Real is one team from Madrid

explanation.surface: A football side, a Madrid outfit, full of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one from Madrid' looks like a person; it is another team, Real Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal is an adjective meaning relating to the stars, as in sidereal time.

clue.text: Shapes I'm busting to get attention

indicators.note: busting means breaking apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone is breaking out of their outfit to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busting' breaks up SHAPESIM to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is special importance or attention given to something, so the two words overlap in sense.

clue.text: Dangerous to shave bottom close to heater in living room

indicators.note: shaving the bottom of a down answer trims off its final letter

parts.note: parlous means dangerous or precarious

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of heater

explanation.surface: Shaving your backside near a heater in the lounge is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: PARLOUS loses its last letter, then R ends heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlour is an old-fashioned word for a sitting room, where a household relaxes.

clue.text: Try to get alcoholic drink put in dessert from the east

indicators.note: put in says the drink is placed inside the dessert
in an across answer reading from the east means right to left, so the dessert is turned round

parts.note: pud is British short for pudding, a dessert
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Rum gets poured into a pudding coming from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns PUD into DUP, and 'put in' places RUM inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum up business or support is to try to solicit or obtain it.

clue.text: Pick imitation nursing attire, 50% off

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the imitation holds the other letters

parts.note: a mock item is an imitation

indicators.note: half the word is cut, leaving its first three of six letters

explanation.surface: Fake nurses' uniforms with half the price knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like a verb but is the tool; 'nursing' puts ATT, half of attire, inside MOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattock is a digging tool like a pickaxe, with a broad blade.

clue.text: Shelter in rocks at foot of mountain

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a slope

indicators.note: in a down answer the foot is the bottom, so the last letter of mountain

explanation.surface: Taking cover among the stones at the base of a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a barrier that shields or protects, as does a shelter.

clue.text: Local restorer restored railroad ride

indicators.note: restored means put back together, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood craftsman has refurbished an old railway attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges LOCALRESTORER.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster is a fairground ride of small cars running on a steep looping track, hence a railroad ride.

clue.text: Objections about displaying butt

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for objections is written backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Complaints about showing one's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BUTS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub and a butt are both the leftover end of a cigarette.

clue.text: Box, perhaps containing old chief's foot

indicators.note: containing says the tree holds the other letters inside

parts.note: box is one example of a tree, hence perhaps
CH is an abbreviation for chief

explanation.surface: A box holding the foot of a former leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container; it is the box tree. 'containing' puts O and CH inside TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical foot of one stressed then one unstressed syllable.

clue.text: Grant possibly picked up for cast

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is the sound of the name

parts.note: Hugh Grant is an English film actor, so Hugh is one Grant

explanation.surface: Grant may have been chosen for the film's cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests actors, matching Hugh Grant; it is a tinge of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is a tinge or shade of colour, as is a hue.

clue.text: Look to wear green pants soon

indicators.note: the other letters wear the word, as clothing goes around a body
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of green are rearranged

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A look that involves putting on green trousers, quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' (British slang for awful) rearranges GREEN into ERENG, and 'to wear' puts LO inside: ERE-LO-NG.
explanation.definitionFit: Erelong is an archaic adverb meaning before long, shortly.

clue.text: British demand queue for boundary

parts.note: to order is to demand
a line is a queue

explanation.surface: Britain insists people form an orderly queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderline is the dividing line between two areas or states, so a boundary.

clue.text: Pretending to be undressed, or similar

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of the outer covering, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: faking means pretending

explanation.surface: Someone is putting on an act of being naked, or something close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undressed' strips FAKING of its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related or alike, so of a similar kind.
